newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in dull trade on Tuesday, with most traders sidelined ahead of the outcome of a U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and the release of the July housing starts report, dealers said.
Housing starts for July were forecast to be around 1.46 million annualised units compared with 1.452 million units reported in June.
"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning except for some position adjustments at the long end," a local dealer said.

"Some traders were waiting for possible direction from the outcome of the FOMC meeting and housing starts figures. But I don't think there will be much impact unless the numbers are way off market expectations," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday, Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed were unchanged from Monday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 and six-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent.
Twelve-months eased 1/16 percentage point to 6 5-7/8 percent.
